text:
sam: Ran a focused attention kernel sweep this morning across H100/A100/L40s. seqlen sweep 128/512/1024/2048/4096, batch sizes 1/2/4, KV cache toggled. Found a weird regression when KV cache + prefetching hits on H100 for long seqs. :eyes:

nina: Ugh, details? numbers? link to logs? :mag:

sam: Short summary: on H100 with KV caching enabled and prefetch turned on we see ~12-19% higher p99 latency vs baseline for seqlen 2048/4096 at bs=1. A100 and L40s unaffected. Throughput similar but tails spike. Repro steps:```bash
./bench_tool --model gpt2-like --gpu h100 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-cache on --kv-prefetch true --runs 50 > h100_kv_prefetch_4096.log
```
raw perf snippet from nvprof (aggregated ms per token):
```
kernel: flash_paged_variant_v2  -> 0.92 ms/token
kernel: fused_flash_small      -> 0.78 ms/token
KV prefetch (= page walk)       -> 0.18 ms/token
Total observed tail p99         -> 1.40 ms/token (vs baseline 1.22)
```

mike: Do we know which selector rule picked paged_flash_variant_v2? sounds like selector favored paged-flash when KV pages present.

sam: Yes selector logs show prefetched_kv_pages > 0 triggers "prefer_paged_flash" rule at heuristic threshold TH_KV_PAGES >= 2. On H100 that rule pushes to paged variant which seems to have worse warp efficiency for >2048 seqs.

ava: Can you paste the selector trace? even the small log lines are fine. Also did you try disabling prefetch?

sam: Selector trace excerpt:```text
[selector] seq=4096 bs=1 kv_pages=3 hw=h100 -> score_paged_flash=0.79 score_fused_flash=0.68 select=paged_flash_variant_v2
[selector] fallback on oom? no -> final=paged_flash_variant_v2
```
With prefetch off the p99 matches baseline. With prefetch on but kv_pages=1 the selector still picked fused in some runs — so it's borderline.

raj: Curious that only H100 shows regression. Could be kernel launch overhead differences or differing L2 behavior. Did you capture SASS counters or sm_efficiency?

sam: Collected nsight traces. H100 shows lower achieved occupancy for paged variant at long seqs and more divergent instruction stalls. A100 occupancy was higher for same kernel. Quick numbers: H100 sm_eff 64% vs A100 78% for paged variant @4096.

nina: So options: 1) change selector heuristic (raise kv_pages threshold to 4 or require seq<2048 to pick paged), 2) tweak paged_flash kernel for H100 path, 3) prefer fused_flash for >2048 on H100. Which should we try first for a patch?

mike: I'd vote for a conservative selector fix first (heuristic). Fast to roll and easy to validate: increase TH_KV_PAGES from 2->4 and add a seq cap (only pick paged when seq<=2048). If that fixes p99 we can schedule kernel optimization separately. :+1:

ava: Agreed. Also add an opt-in env var to force paged_flash to collect extra perf counters when enabled so we can iterate on kernel later.

sam: I'll open a small PR for the selector tweak and integration test with our microbenchmark. Proposed patch:```diff
- if (kv_pages >= 2) prefer = PAGED_FLASH;
+ if (kv_pages >= 4 && seq_len <= 2048) prefer = PAGED_FLASH;
```
I'll run quick canary on dedicated pool once merged.

deploy-bot: CanCI: test/smoke-attn-kernel (h100) queued by sam.

sam: Also pinging @nina/@raj to run a targeted Nsight capture on paged_flash_variant_v2 with prefetch enabled on H100 when you have cycles. I attached the small perf tarball to #artifacts (link: https://internal.redwood/artifacts/h100_kv_prefetch_4096.tar.gz)

raj: Will do later today. If the selector patch is safe we should ship to canary 1 and monitor p99, cost delta. Also add a metric for "selector_switch_count" per model so we can see how often paged vs fused are chosen in prod.

nina: Quick note: also saw a tiny increase in memory bandwidth on H100 runs which might hint prefetch traffic interfering with main traffic. We'll check PCIe vs NVLINK patterns.

sam: Thanks all. Action items: sam PR for selector tweak + microbench, raj run Nsight capture and share, nina investigate BW traces, mike/ava add opt-in perf flag. I'll post results in this thread. :rocket:

ava: acked. If the change is trivial we can hotfix dedicated pool tonight.

sam: last: observed regression only on bsz=1. bsz=2/4 knobs look fine (less tail). Probably because batching masks the kernel inefficiency. Good for canary plan.

mike: perfect, keep the logs coming.
